question: Double fertilisation is the characteristic of:
solution:
The correct answer is** "angiosperm".** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Double fertilization is a first-rate function of flowering plants **(angiosperms).**** **
 
• **Angiosperm**, additionally known as a flowering plant, is any of approximately **300,000** species of flowering plants, the biggest and maximum numerous institution in the country **Plantae. ** 
 
• Angiosperms constitute about **eighty per cent** of all of the recognized inexperienced flowers now living. 
 
• The angiosperms are vascular seed vegetation in which the ovule **(egg)** is fertilized and develops properly right into a seed in an enclosed hollow ovary.
 
• The** ovary** itself is normally enclosed in a flower, a part of the angiospermous plant that carries the male or lady reproductive organs or both. 
 
• Fruits are derived from the maturing floral organs of the angiospermous plant and are consequently a feature of angiosperms. 
 
• By contrast, in gymnosperms (e.g., **conifers** and **cycads**), the opposite massive organization of vascular seed plants, the seeds do now no longer expand enclosed inside an ovary but are commonly borne uncovered at the surfaces of reproductive structures, which include cones.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fungi:**

 
 
• ​A fungus (**fungi**) is any member of the group of **eukaryotic **organisms that includes microorganisms such as **yeasts** and **moulds**, as well as the more familiar mushrooms. 
 
• These organisms are labelled as a **kingdom**, one after the other from the alternative eukaryotic kingdoms, which through one conventional category encompass **Plantae, Animalia, Protozoa**, and **Chromista.** 
 
• A feature that locations fungi in a one-of-a-kind nation from **plants, bacteria**, and a few **protists** are chitin of their molecular walls. 
 
• Fungi, like animals, are **heterotrophs**; they collect their meals by soaking up dissolved molecules, normally through secreting digestive enzymes into their environment. 
 
• Fungi do now no longer **photosynthesize**. 
 
• Growth is their approach to mobility, besides spores (some of which might be **flagellated**), which may also journey thru the air or water.Fungi are the essential decomposers in ecological systems.
 
 
 
• **Algae: **
 
 
• **Algae** is a casual time period for a massive and various organization of **photosynthetic** eukaryotic organisms. 
 
• It is a polyphyletic grouping that consists of species from more than one wonderful **clade.** 
 
• Included organisms variety from unicellular **microalgae**, which includes **Chlorella, Prototheca** and the **diatoms**, to multicellular forms, which include the massive kelp, a big brown alga that might also additionally develop as much as **50** metres (**a hundred and sixty ft**) in length. 
 
• Most are **aquatic** and **autotrophic** (they generate food internally) and lack many of the distinct cell and tissue types, such as** stomata**, **xylem** and **phloem** that are found in land plants. 
 
 
 
• ​ **Gymnosperms:**
 
 
• The **gymnosperms** are a group of seed-producing plants that includes **conifers, cycads, Ginkgo**, and **gnetophytes**, forming the clade **Gymnospermae**. 
 
• The term gymnosperm comes from the composite word in Greek, literally meaning '**naked seeds**'. 
 
• The name is based on the unenclosed condition of their seeds (called** ovules** in their unfertilized state). 
 
• The non-encased condition of their seeds contrasts with the seeds and ovules of flowering plants (**angiosperms**), which are enclosed within an ovary.
